name: Hydrogen Ground State
description: A single hydrogen atom: 1 proton and 1 electron in the 1s orbital

layman.title: The Simplest Atom
layman.summary: Meet hydrogen — the most basic building block of the universe

sections.whatsHappening: You're looking at a single hydrogen atom — the simplest atom that exists. At the center is a proton (red), a positively charged particle. Surrounding it is a cloud of probability (blue) showing where the electron is most likely to be found. The electron isn't orbiting like a planet — it exists as a fuzzy cloud of possibility.
sections.whyItMatters: Hydrogen makes up about 75% of all matter in the universe. Every star, including our Sun, is mostly hydrogen. Understanding this one atom is the foundation for understanding all of chemistry and most of physics.
sections.whatToWatch: Notice the blue cloud around the proton. This is the electron's '1s orbital' — a spherical shape meaning the electron could be found anywhere around the proton with roughly equal probability. The denser inner region shows where the electron is most likely to be.
sections.funFact: If a hydrogen atom were the size of a football stadium, the proton would be a marble at the 50-yard line. The electron cloud would fill the entire stadium. Atoms are almost entirely empty space!

scientific.narrative: The hydrogen atom is shown in its ground state with principal quantum number n=1, angular momentum quantum number l=0, and magnetic quantum number m=0. The electron probability density is given by the square of the 1s wavefunction, which is spherically symmetric. The radial probability peaks at the Bohr radius (52.9 pm from the nucleus).
